title: Best SBA Lending Software in 2026
summary: Seven SBA lending software platforms compared on 7(a) and 504 support, E-Tran, underwriting and AI, with what each does and which SBA lender it fits.
body_markdown:
Quick answer


SBA lending software takes a 7(a) or 504 loan from application to decision, and often through closing and servicing. Choose by where your hours go. If the bottleneck is SBA workflow, forms and E-Tran submission, look at Lenders Cooperative, nCino, Abrigo, Baker Hill or SPARK. If it is the underwriting on each file, reading the package, spreading the borrower and guarantors and writing the memo, look at Kita or Aloan.


Key takeaways


Most SBA platforms organize the loan: checklists, SBA forms, E-Tran submission, closing documents and servicing. Fewer of them do the credit analysis on the file itself.


Of the seven platforms here, only Lenders Cooperative states support for 7(a) and 504 through closing and servicing. nCino, Abrigo, Baker Hill and SPARK describe 7(a) support and E-Tran integration.


SBA launched iCAP on November 5, 2026 to replace E-Tran, and lenders must move off the E-Tran origination interface by June 2027. Ask every vendor about its iCAP plans.


**Best for SBA underwriting:** Kita, which collects the package, checks every document, spreads the financials and drafts a cited memo on 7(a) and 504 files, inside your LOS or in Intelligent LOS.


SBA lending software runs the work on a loan the U.S. Small Business Administration guarantees. A lender making 7(a) or 504 loans needs to collect a long package, confirm eligibility, spread the business and its guarantors, write a credit memo, generate SBA forms, submit the guaranty request and, after closing, service and report on the loan. Each platform below covers a different share of that list.


The platforms split into two groups. Origination platforms move the SBA loan through its stages and connect to SBA’s systems. Underwriting platforms do the credit analysis inside those stages, and a newer set uses AI to read the documents and draft the memo. Several lenders run one of each.


This guide compares seven of them. Each competitor entry uses only what the vendor states on its own site or in its press releases, cited in the references at the end and checked on November 14, 2026. Kita is our product, and its entry uses only what kita.ai states.


## SBA lending software compared


The scorecard lines up the seven platforms on the jobs an SBA lender needs done. An X means the vendor’s site does not say it, which does not prove the product cannot do it. Ask the vendor.

01


## nCino


Best for banks standardizing SBA on an enterprise platform


nCino sells a cloud banking platform to banks and credit unions. Its SBA Solution runs SBA loans inside that platform, and nCino says it supports the approval process for any type of SBA loan, including 7(a) and Express.\[6,7,8\]


-


**E-Tran from inside the platform.** Lenders submit SBA loan guaranty requests to E-Tran from within nCino, then keep sending updated data until SBA approves or rejects the loan and assigns a loan number.


-


**SBA forms and closing documents.** nCino creates and maps the SBA Loan Authorization and SBA Express Loan Authorization, supports e-signed forms such as Form 1919 and 4506-C through DocuSign, and generates 7(a) closing documents through document prep integrations.


-


**AI through Banking Advisor and partners.** Banking Advisor, generally available since June 2024, drafts deal and credit memo narratives. In October 2026 nCino announced it will resell Parlay’s AI intake system for SBA lenders.


Best for:


Banks and larger credit unions that already run nCino, or plan to, and want SBA 7(a) and Express loans in the same system of record as the rest of the commercial book.


02


## Abrigo


Best for community banks adding SBA 7(a) to an existing Abrigo stack


Abrigo makes lending and credit risk software for banks and credit unions. Its SBA lending product, sold under the Sageworks name, handles SBA 7(a) underwriting and decisioning in the same platform as the institution’s other loans.\[9,10\]


-


**E-Tran and SBA forms.** Abrigo integrates with E-Tran through the Sageworks API network and produces SBA Forms 1919 and 1920 as PDFs, so staff do not key the same data twice.


-


**One platform for every loan type.** SBA, commercial and consumer loans sit on one platform. One customer on Abrigo’s page reports exporting 318 loans totaling $26,712,263 to E-Tran and receiving SBA approval.


-


**Abrigo Lending Assistant.** An AI assistant that imports data from unstructured documents such as financial statements and debt schedules, checks submitted documents against what was requested, and drafts editable credit narratives. Abrigo says narratives are 25% faster.


Best for:


Community banks and credit unions that already spread and decision commercial loans in Abrigo and want SBA 7(a) in the same workflow.


03


## Lenders Cooperative


Best for 7(a) and 504 lenders that want software plus an outsourced SBA team


Lenders Cooperative runs a cloud lending platform for small business, SBA and commercial loans, from digital application through closing and servicing. In February 2025 it completed its merger with Ventures Lending Technologies, a provider of SBA 504 and 7(a) origination and servicing software for nearly two decades.\[11,12,13,14\]


-


**SBA workflow end to end.** Workflows cover 7(a) MARC lines, guaranty selection, Form 1919 and E-Tran submission, followed by closing documents for every state and boarding to servicing and the lender’s core.


-


**504 through Ventures.** Lenders Cooperative reports that the Ventures platform processed 99.8% of SBA 504 loans in 2024. Ventures stays in use and SBA-compliant while the unified platform adds 504 and servicing.


-


**Outsourced SBA services.** Its SBA Lender Service Provider team works with banks and credit unions on 7(a) and 504 loans, covering eligibility, underwriting, E-Tran submission, servicing, 1502 reporting and guaranty purchase support, in full or a la carte.


-


**AI under underwriter control.** The platform uses AI in document review, spreading and credit narratives.


Best for:


Banks, credit unions and CDCs that make both 7(a) and 504 loans and want one vendor for the platform, closing, servicing and extra underwriting capacity.


04


## Baker Hill


Best for banks running scored and judgmental small business lending


Baker Hill makes loan origination software for small business and commercial lending. In November 2025 it launched UN/FY, which brings small business lending, deposit account opening and AI tools into one system and replaces the NextGen brand. UN/FY lists scored, judgmental and SBA lending.\[15,16,17,18\]


-


**E-Tran integration.** Baker Hill added SBA E-Tran integration for loan submission to its NextGen platform in 2020.


-


**AI spreading and document classification.** Its ASK BKR AI tool classifies documents and spreads financials automatically. Baker Hill says AI-driven automation cuts origination costs by up to 60%.


-


**Used by an active 7(a) lender.** In June 2026 Beacon Bank, whose 44 Business Capital division is one of the most active SBA 7(a) lenders, expanded its use of UN/FY for small business and SBA lending.


Best for:


Community and regional banks that run high volumes of small business loans, a mix of scored and judgmental credit, and want SBA in the same origination system.


05


## SPARK


Best for SBA-focused lenders that want SBA tooling included


SPARK is a small business lending platform from Ignify Technologies, a public benefit corporation, for banks, lender service providers and mission-driven lenders that originate SBA and other small business loans. Ignify reports more than $8 billion in loans funded on SPARK.\[19,20\]


-


**SBA tools included.** E-Tran integration, SBA 10 Tabs and automatic SBA form generation come with no extra cost or customization, and the platform checks SBA eligibility natively.


-


**Spreading inside the credit memo.** SPARK spreads business tax returns, income statements and balance sheets automatically and can embed the spreads in the lender’s credit memo template.


-


**Applicant portal and integrations.** A borrower portal requests and collects documents, and SPARK integrates with more than 15 providers, including DocuSign and MeridianLink.


Best for:


Banks and lender service providers whose small business book leans on SBA 7(a) and that want SBA-specific workflow without paying for customization.


06


## Aloan


Best for AI-assisted SBA underwriting at community banks


Aloan describes itself as an AI-native commercial LOS for community banks and credit unions. Its SBA product is built for 7(a), 504 and Express teams and runs as the lender’s LOS or alongside an existing one through REST APIs and webhooks.\[21,22\]


-


**Guarantor spreading with K-1 tracing.** Aloan classifies the SBA package and spreads the borrower and every guarantor, tracing K-1s across affiliates.


-


**Source-cited memo.** It assembles the credit memo with each figure cited to its source page, and the lender keeps eligibility, SOP interpretation and the approval.


-


**Fast setup.** Aloan says most lenders go live in two to four weeks, and that customers report 77% less time per standard commercial file.


Best for:


Community banks and credit unions that want AI to do the SBA spreading and memo work and are prepared to keep E-Tran submission, closing and servicing in other systems, since Aloan’s pages do not list them.


07


## Kita


Best for underwriting the hard SBA file, from package to cited memo


Kita is the AI-native stack for modern underwriting, configured to each lender’s loan products and credit policy. On an SBA 7(a) or 504 file it collects the package, checks every document, spreads the financials and drafts a credit memo with every figure cited to its source. Your underwriter makes the decision.


-


**AI Credit Officer.** Messages the borrower on WhatsApp, SMS or email in 30+ languages, asks for the exact documents an SBA package needs, checks each upload as it lands and follows up until the file is complete.


-


**Kita Capture.** Reads SBA forms, tax returns and bank statements in any format, including scans and photos. That covers Form 1919, personal financial statements, 1120 and 1120-S returns, Schedule C, K-1s and 941s. It flags tampering and catches contradictions across the file.


-


**AI Underwriter.** Builds a period-over-period spread, computes debt service coverage, margin and trend, holds the file against your encoded credit policy and drafts the memo with every figure linked to the document line it came from.


-


**Change-of-ownership files.** Prepares and reconciles full acquisition packages, including the cash proof that SOP 50 10 8.1 requires inside a Quality of Earnings report. Kita is not a valuer and does not write the Quality of Earnings report.


-


**Intelligent LOS or your current LOS.** Kita is API-first and works inside the LOS you already use, or runs origination from application to decision in Intelligent LOS, with REST APIs and a webhook on every loan-file event.


-


**Auditable.** SOC 2 Type II compliant and ISO 27001 certified. Every policy check is recorded and a named person signs the decision.


Best for:


SBA lenders, including CDFIs, credit unions and community banks, whose bottleneck is the document and analysis work on each 7(a) or 504 file. Kita’s pages do not list E-Tran submission, closing documents or servicing, so those stay in your LOS.


## How to choose SBA lending software


Six questions separate these products more than any feature list:


-


**Which SBA programs you make.** A 7(a) loan goes up to $5 million and can fund working capital, equipment, real estate and changes of ownership. A 504 loan goes up to $5.5 million for major fixed assets and is made by a Certified Development Company together with a senior lender.\[1,2\] Few platforms state support for both, so confirm 504 if you lend through a CDC.


-


**Where the hours go.** If staff spend their time on SBA forms, checklists and resubmissions, a workflow platform with E-Tran and form generation helps most. If they spend it reading tax returns, spreading guarantors and writing memos, look for software that does that analysis and shows its sources.


-


**E-Tran today, iCAP next.** Lenders submit loan guaranty requests to SBA online.\[3\] SBA says the 7(a) origination API in iCAP becomes available in December 2026, all lenders get iCAP origination access by January 1, 2027, and migration from the E-Tran origination interface is required by June 2027.\[4\] None of the vendor pages we checked mention iCAP yet.


-


**The 2026 change-of-ownership rules.** SOP 50 10 8.1 took effect on October 1, 2026. It requires a Quality of Earnings report, including a cash proof, for initial acquisitions and business expansions priced at $3 million or more.\[5\] Ask how each system handles that reconciliation.[Here is what Appendix 15 asks of lenders](https://www.kita.ai/blog/sba-sop-50-10-8-1-change-of-ownership) .


-


**Whether you keep your LOS.** Some products replace the origination system. Others work through an API inside the one you run, which avoids a migration but splits the file across two systems.


-


**Whose numbers they are.** Nearly every figure in this market is vendor-reported. Ask to run the product on a few of your own closed SBA files before you sign.


In practice, a lender that wants one vendor for 7(a) and 504 workflow, closing, servicing and outsourced help will look first at Lenders Cooperative. A bank already on nCino, Abrigo or Baker Hill will usually add SBA to the platform it has. A lender that wants SBA tooling included at no extra cost can compare SPARK. A lender whose underwriters are the bottleneck should look at Kita or Aloan, and can keep its current LOS for E-Tran, closing and servicing.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best SBA lending software?


It depends on which part of the SBA process slows you down. For SBA workflow and E-Tran submission, Lenders Cooperative covers 7(a) and 504 through closing and servicing, and nCino, Abrigo, Baker Hill and SPARK support 7(a) and E-Tran inside a wider lending platform. For the underwriting work on each file, collecting the package, checking documents, spreading and drafting the memo, Kita and Aloan use AI to do that analysis, and Kita can sit inside the LOS you already run.


### What does SBA lending software do?


SBA lending software runs a 7(a) or 504 loan from application to decision and, in many products, through closing and servicing. Depending on the vendor that means collecting the package, checking eligibility, spreading the financials, drafting the credit memo, generating SBA forms such as Form 1919, submitting the guaranty request to SBA and reporting on the loan afterwards.


### What is the best software for underwriting SBA 7(a) and 504 loans?


For the underwriting itself, choose software that reads the whole package, spreads the borrower and guarantors and drafts a memo you can check line by line. Kita does this on 7(a) and 504 files: it collects the documents, checks them for fraud, builds the spread, applies your credit policy and drafts a memo with every figure cited to its source, and your underwriter decides. Aloan also does AI spreading and memo work for 7(a), 504 and Express.


### Does SBA lending software have to connect to E-Tran?


Lenders submit 7(a) guaranty requests to SBA online, so five of the seven platforms here integrate with E-Tran. That is changing. SBA launched iCAP on November 5, 2026 to replace E-Tran and CAFS, with a 7(a) origination API due in December 2026 and migration from the E-Tran origination interface required by June 2027. Ask each vendor when it will support iCAP.


### Can AI underwrite an SBA loan?


AI can do most of the work and should not make the decision. It can collect and read the package, reconcile figures across tax returns and bank statements, spread the financials, test the file against the lender’s policy and draft the memo. The lender is responsible for the credit decision, so a person should review the file and sign it. Kita and Aloan both leave the decision with the lender.


### What is the difference between SBA loan origination software and SBA underwriting software?


Origination software manages the loan’s path: the application, checklists, SBA forms, E-Tran submission, closing documents and boarding to servicing. Underwriting software does the credit analysis inside that path: reading the documents, spreading the financials, calculating debt service coverage and drafting the memo. Some platforms do both. Kita does the underwriting work and can run inside an existing LOS or as the full system through Intelligent LOS.


### Do we have to replace our LOS to use Kita for SBA underwriting?


No. Kita is API-first and integrates into an existing loan origination system, credit engine or custom workflow, so the system you use for E-Tran submission, closing and servicing stays in place. Lenders who want one system for application to decision can run it in Kita’s Intelligent LOS.
